title: A Side Hustle Must Pass the Net-Income Test
meta_description: Test side-hustle demand, unit economics, total hours, tax, legal risk and scam exposure before revenue screenshots waste cash and time.

sections.heading: Revenue Is Not the Result
paragraphs: A side hustle is often advertised with a revenue screenshot: $2,000 in sales, a fully booked weekend or a platform balance climbing overnight. None of those figures proves that the work improved the household. The useful result is cash collected minus operating costs, tax provision, unpaid labor and the risk attached to earning it.

The first filter is therefore net income, not excitement. Track money received, refunds, platform fees, payment processing, materials, shipping, mileage, insurance, software, advertising, licenses, professional help and equipment wear. Then divide what remains by every hour required, including sales, administration, travel and correction work.

A venture can be worthwhile below a normal hourly wage when it deliberately buys training, a portfolio or future capacity. That exception must be written and time-limited. Calling every loss an investment lets an untested hobby consume cash indefinitely while success remains impossible to measure.

Set the objective before choosing the idea. Is the goal $500 of monthly household cash, a path out of one employer, seasonal debt repayment, proof of customer demand or a creative practice that partly pays for itself? Different objectives require different prices, hours and stop rules.

Protect the primary income source. Review employment agreements, confidentiality, intellectual property, non-solicitation, schedule and conflict rules before accepting work. Never use employer time, data, customers, equipment or proprietary methods without written authorization. Ethical separation is a business control, not bureaucracy.

The opening photograph shows remote freelance work because the first test is operational reality: a laptop, devices, time and attention must produce an identifiable customer outcome. Online access alone does not create a business, and flexibility claims should be tested against the actual delivery schedule.

Use a separate ledger from day one even if a separate legal entity is unnecessary. Record date, customer, service or product, gross amount, fees, direct cost, mileage, payment status and time. A business account may improve separation where appropriate, but clean records begin with consistent classification.

Do not borrow heavily to prove an idea. Cap the pilot loss at an amount the household can absorb without touching rent, tax money, emergency reserves or retirement accounts. Equipment should follow paid demand wherever possible, not precede it because buying tools feels like progress.

Write three thresholds: minimum net dollars per month, minimum effective hourly rate and maximum weekly hours. Add a trial end date. The filters make it possible to reject an opportunity that produces impressive activity but weak economics.

A valid side hustle should make the household more resilient, not merely busier. It can pass by producing useful cash, durable skill or verified market access. It fails when costs, fatigue and concentration are hidden behind gross sales.

Create a one-page opportunity statement before spending: customer, promised outcome, price, direct cost, acquisition route, delivery hours, major risk and evidence deadline. If these fields cannot be stated plainly, research is incomplete. The page becomes the baseline against which later enthusiasm, scope changes and spending are judged.

sections.heading: Find a Paying Problem Before Building a Brand
paragraphs: Demand is evidence that a defined customer will pay for a defined outcome. Compliments, followers and survey enthusiasm are weaker than deposits, completed sales or repeat orders. Start with the customer’s problem, current alternative, purchase trigger and acceptable delivery method before choosing colors, a logo or social account.

The Small Business Administration recommends market research on demand, market size, location, saturation and the prices customers pay for alternatives. [[S2|Its planning guidance]] makes competitive analysis a profitability input, not a branding exercise.

Interview people who fit the proposed customer, but ask about behavior rather than predictions. What did they buy last time? What did it cost? Why was the alternative inadequate? A person can sincerely say an idea sounds excellent and still never allocate money to it.

Define one narrow offer with scope, price, turnaround, revision limit and customer responsibility. “I do marketing” cannot be tested. “I will audit a local retailer’s email welcome sequence and deliver five prioritized changes within four days for $350” creates a purchase decision and a delivery boundary.

Pre-sell ethically. Explain that the offer is a pilot, state what is included and refund when promised work cannot be delivered. Do not fabricate scarcity, testimonials or prior clients. Early customers are not consent to receive a lower standard; they deserve transparent terms.

Estimate reachable demand rather than total market headlines. Ten million possible buyers mean little when the operator can contact twenty suitable prospects or serve only one neighborhood. Build a list of actual acquisition channels and calculate how many conversations are needed for one sale.

Search behavior and competitor reviews can expose unmet needs, but do not copy protected work or misrepresent another company. Use public information to understand price, delivery, complaints and positioning. Compete through a clearer outcome, better service or a defensible specialty.

Choose service before product when it permits cheaper validation. A service can reveal language, objections and willingness to pay before inventory. Product businesses can also pilot with small batches, samples or preorders, subject to consumer, platform and fulfillment obligations.

Separate purchaser from user. A parent may pay for tutoring used by a student; a business owner may buy work used by employees. The offer must satisfy the decision maker’s budget and the user’s experience. Confusing them makes otherwise useful research misleading.

Demand is not proven by one friend’s discounted purchase. Seek several independent customers, at least one repeat or referral signal, and a sale at the intended price. Set the evidence standard before launch so affection and sunk cost cannot lower it later.

A waitlist is evidence only when names are qualified and the next action is explicit. Ask permission to contact prospects with a priced offer by a stated date. Large email counts assembled through giveaways can exaggerate demand because the incentive attracted attention to the free item rather than the paid outcome.

sections.heading: Price from Unit Economics, Not Competitor Envy
paragraphs: Price must cover variable cost, a share of fixed cost, nonbillable time, risk and owner compensation. Matching the cheapest competitor can lock in a model that works only because the operator ignores labor, already owns subsidized equipment or earns elsewhere.

For a product, contribution margin per unit is selling price minus costs that rise with each sale: materials, packaging, payment fees, marketplace commission, fulfillment and expected returns. For a service, include subcontractors, per-client software, travel and the delivery hours consumed.

The SBA defines break-even as the point where total revenue equals total cost and gives the unit formula as fixed costs divided by price minus variable cost. [[S2|Its startup-cost guidance]] also recommends identifying one-time, fixed and variable expenses before launch.

Assume a service charges $300, incurs $30 of direct cost and needs six delivery hours plus two hours of sales and administration. Contribution before fixed cost is $270 and the pre-tax effective rate is $33.75 per hour. A promised “$50 hourly rate” based only on delivery time would be false.

Include failed acquisition. If five unpaid consultations produce one client, the successful job must carry its share of all five conversations. Track leads, qualified conversations, proposals, wins and acquisition hours. Advertising spend is only one customer-acquisition cost.

Annualize equipment over realistic use instead of charging the full laptop to the first customer or pretending it is free. Keep tax accounting separate from management economics: a permitted deduction schedule does not tell whether buying the equipment was commercially sensible.

Model refunds, chargebacks, damage, rework and nonpayment using observed rates when available. A zero-loss forecast is not conservative merely because problems have not happened in a tiny sample. Add a clear contingency until enough operating data replaces it.

Use at least three volumes: low, expected and capacity limit. Fixed software may be harmless at twenty clients and destructive at two. High volume may require help, storage, insurance or a platform plan that changes the cost structure. Unit economics can shift as sales grow.

Discount only for a defined exchange such as lower scope, advance payment, a case-study permission or a batch commitment. Permanent “introductory” pricing trains customers to expect work below the sustainable rate and leaves no evidence about the real offer.

The price test passes when expected volume covers all operating costs, pays a chosen labor floor and leaves a tax reserve without relying on future scale. Growth can improve economics; it should not be required to make every current sale rational.

Distinguish cash flow from profit. Advance payments can make the bank balance look strong before delivery cost is incurred, while late-paying customers can make profitable work difficult to finance. Forecast when deposits arrive and when materials, contractors, refunds and tax leave, then maintain enough buffer to fulfill every accepted order.

sections.heading: Count Every Hour the Customer Never Sees
paragraphs: Side work competes with sleep, family, recovery, exercise and primary employment. The relevant denominator includes prospecting, messaging, preparation, delivery, travel, bookkeeping, procurement, support, refunds and learning required to meet the promised standard.

Keep a time log in fifteen- or thirty-minute blocks during the pilot. Memory consistently drops fragmented administration. Tag hours as acquisition, delivery, operations and development. After four weeks, calculate net income per total hour and per delivery hour; the gap shows overhead.

Set a capacity ceiling before demand arrives. If the business has eight weekly hours, reserve some for administration and recovery. Selling ten delivery hours creates late work or broken promises. Scarcity should lead to a waitlist, higher price or reduced scope—not hidden overtime.

Price irregular schedules differently from predictable blocks. A two-hour event can consume travel, setup and an unusable gap. On-call tasks fragment evenings even when no customer appears. Compensation must reflect controlled time, not only active minutes.

Test energy as well as duration. Two hours of complex work after a demanding shift may be unsafe or low quality. Schedule the hardest tasks in realistic conditions during the pilot. A plan that works only with permanent exhaustion is not viable.

Include caregiving and purchased support. If side work requires childcare, transport or meals that would not otherwise occur, those costs belong in the economics. Unpaid help from a partner is still labor and should be agreed, recorded and valued.

Protect a no-work period each week. Recovery is a capacity control, not laziness. Fatigue raises mistakes, driving risk, customer conflict and primary-job damage. The side hustle should fit around a life rather than consume every unpriced hour.

Compare the effective rate with alternatives. Overtime, a raise, training for a higher-paid role or selling unused items may produce more cash with less setup. Entrepreneurship is one income tool, not a moral requirement.

Add commute and vehicle economics for delivery or field work: business miles, fuel, maintenance, depreciation, cleaning, tolls and deadhead travel. A platform’s gross hourly display can omit the return trip and waiting time.

The time filter passes when the work meets the hourly floor under ordinary conditions, stays inside the capacity ceiling and leaves primary obligations intact. A temporary launch sprint must have an end date and recovery plan.

Use a replacement-cost test for owner labor. Ask what a qualified person would charge to complete the same work at the required quality. If the model fails after a reasonable labor allowance, it is not ready to support delegation or become a reliable income source, even if unpaid owner effort currently hides the weakness.

sections.heading: Build Tax and Records into the Price
paragraphs: Gig income is generally taxable even when work is temporary, paid in cash or not accompanied by an information form. The IRS says workers should track income and receipts and may need estimated payments when treated as independent contractors. [[S1|Its gig-work guidance]] should be reviewed before spending the gross deposit.

Create a tax holding account or ledger category and move a planning percentage from each receipt. The correct amount depends on total household income, deductions, state rules and other taxes; obtain current professional advice rather than using one internet percentage as law.

The IRS notes that a person with wages and gig income may be able to increase withholding at the employee job instead of making separate estimated payments. That method can simplify cash flow, but the calculation still needs current income and the official estimator or Form 1040-ES guidance.

Record income from every channel, including cash, tips, barter where taxable and platform payments. An information-reporting threshold is not an income exclusion. Reconcile platform statements to bank deposits, fees, refunds and gross reportable amounts.

Save receipts with business purpose, date, vendor, amount and payment method. A bank line alone may not explain what was purchased. Keep mileage and mixed-use allocations contemporaneously. Deduct only ordinary, necessary and properly supported business expenses under current rules.

The mid-article photograph shows a person checking receipts because bookkeeping is part of product cost. If administration is excluded from hours and tax is excluded from cash planning, the side hustle’s stated return is overstated twice.

Do not form an entity solely because social media says an LLC creates deductions. The SBA explains that structure affects taxes, paperwork, fundraising and personal liability. [[S7|Its launch guidance]] also notes that licenses and permits depend on activity and location.

Worker classification is factual, not a box selected for convenience. The Department of Labor’s 2026 proposed framework discusses economic dependence, control and opportunity for profit or loss, while also noting that actual practice matters. [[S6|Current classification guidance]] should be checked because rules can change and other laws use different tests.

Use invoices with legal name, service, date, amount, terms and payment status. Number them consistently. Follow up on receivables promptly and do not count an unpaid invoice as spendable household income.

The tax filter passes when price leaves room for lawful tax, records can support the return and payment timing does not force debt. A profitable business can still cause a cash crisis when the owner spends tax money or ignores quarterly obligations.

Set a monthly close routine: reconcile accounts, match receipts, review unpaid invoices, update mileage, estimate tax and lock a copy of the ledger. Regular closing detects missing income and misclassified costs while records are still recoverable. Back up sensitive files securely and grant access only to people who need it.

sections.heading: Control Legal, Safety and Employer Risk
paragraphs: Before launch, identify licenses, permits, zoning, professional restrictions, product standards, privacy duties and insurance relevant to the activity and location. Requirements differ. “It is only a side hustle” is not an exemption from consumer, tax or safety obligations.

Review the primary employer’s policies in writing. Disclose outside work when required and seek clarification before serving a competitor, vendor or customer. Keep separate devices, storage, accounts and working hours where necessary. Never reuse confidential materials or present employer work as a personal portfolio without permission.

Use a written agreement for material work. Define scope, price, payment schedule, deadlines, revision limits, customer inputs, cancellation, ownership, confidentiality and dispute route. Templates require jurisdiction and activity review; copied clauses can create obligations the operator does not understand.

Collect only customer data needed to deliver the service. Secure accounts with unique credentials and multifactor authentication, restrict access and delete records under a documented retention rule. A tiny business can still harm customers through careless data handling.

Check personal auto, renters or homeowners coverage before assuming business use is protected. Delivery, client visits, inventory and customer property may need different coverage. Ask the insurer directly and retain the answer.

Products require quality control, labeling, returns and recall thinking. Services involving health, children, finance, legal matters, homes or physical safety demand qualified advice and appropriate coverage. Do not offer regulated expertise by adding a disclaimer to unqualified work.

Separate personal and business cash to improve control, but understand that a bank account alone does not create legal protection. Structure, contracts, conduct, insurance and compliance work together. Choose complexity proportional to actual risk.

Write an incident plan: customer injury, lost data, disputed charge, damaged package, missed deadline or platform suspension. List who is contacted, what evidence is retained and which work pauses. A plan reduces improvised promises during stress.

Protect household identity. Use a business contact channel where suitable, avoid publishing a home address unnecessarily, and verify customers before entering private locations. No sale is worth bypassing a safety boundary.

The risk filter passes when the activity can be delivered lawfully, ethically and safely without endangering primary employment or exposing the household to an unbounded loss. If coverage or permission is unclear, pause before taking payment.

Advertising claims are part of risk control. Describe normal, supportable outcomes; disclose important limits; and obtain permission for testimonials and images. Do not promise income, health, financial or performance results that evidence cannot support. Ethical marketing lowers disputes because customers understand what they are actually buying.

sections.heading: Reject Opportunities That Require Belief Instead of Evidence
paragraphs: Side-hustle scams sell urgency, secrecy and effortless income. The Federal Trade Commission warns about unexpected offers, big money for little effort, pressure and demands for upfront payment. [[S3|Its 2026 guidance]] advises researching the company and speaking with current or former workers.

Never pay to unlock wages, recharge a task account or release supposed commissions. The FTC describes task scams that display fake earnings and then demand deposits. A balance inside the scammer’s app is not money controlled by the worker.

Verify the company through contact information found independently. Search its name with “complaint,” “review” and “scam,” but do not treat positive reviews as proof; testimonials can be fake or atypical. Confirm legal identity, payment terms and who bears refunds.

Reject fake-check arrangements. A stranger who sends a check and asks for equipment purchases, gift cards, crypto or money returned is shifting loss to the recipient. Banks can make funds appear available before discovering the check is fraudulent.

Business-opportunity sellers should explain the product, customer, expenses and typical outcome with required disclosures where applicable. Vague automation, secret systems and assured high earnings are not operating models. Independent verification must happen before payment.

Platform work can be legitimate and still concentrated. Track the percentage of revenue from one app, client or algorithm. A suspension, fee change or ranking loss can erase income instantly. Build direct, lawful customer relationships where terms permit and retain portable records.

Beware of inventory loading and recruitment dependence. If earnings require buying packages, recruiting friends or consuming the product personally, calculate customer demand outside the participant network. Revenue generated by recruits is not proof of retail viability.

Protect identification and banking data. Genuine onboarding can require tax information, but confirm the counterparty and secure channel first. Do not send documents to an unsolicited messaging account because a logo looks familiar.
Set a 24-hour cooling period for any upfront spend above the pilot limit. Review terms with an unaffiliated person. Pressure that cannot survive one day of diligence is itself a rejection signal.

The integrity filter passes when customers, work, price, payment and expenses are independently understandable. If profit depends on hiding how money is made, misleading buyers or recruiting someone into the same uncertainty, walk away.

Treat crypto-only payment, communication restricted to encrypted chat and refusal to provide a verifiable contract as combined risk signals, not proof by themselves. Pause when normal diligence is discouraged. Genuine clients and platforms can explain their identity, the work, the approval process and how a worker can withdraw earned funds.

sections.heading: Run a Paid Pilot with Stop Rules
paragraphs: A pilot is not endless preparation. Choose one offer, one customer segment, one acquisition channel, a fixed cash cap and a fixed period—often four to eight weeks. The goal is evidence about demand, delivery, economics and personal capacity.

Define the scorecard before the first sale: qualified leads, conversations, proposals, paid customers, repeat or referral signals, gross revenue, refunds, direct cost, total hours, net cash and tax reserve. Add quality measures relevant to the work.

Require payment evidence. A free project can test delivery but not willingness to pay. If free work is necessary for a portfolio, cap the number, state the exchange and move to the intended price on schedule.

Use a separate pilot budget. Approve each expense against a hypothesis: equipment enables delivery, advertising tests acquisition or insurance controls identified risk. Do not let branding purchases consume the loss cap before customers arrive.

Schedule weekly review, not constant emotional judgment. Compare actual with forecast, identify one constraint and choose one change. Altering audience, offer, price and channel simultaneously destroys the lesson.

Write stop rules such as: no paid customer after twenty qualified conversations, effective hourly rate below the floor after three deliveries, complaints above a threshold, cash cap reached or primary-job performance harmed. Stop rules protect against sunk-cost escalation.

Write continue rules too: several independent customers at target price, positive contribution margin, delivery within capacity, acceptable acquisition effort and at least one repeat or referral signal. Optimism alone does not extend the pilot.

Interview customers after delivery. Ask what triggered purchase, what almost stopped it, what outcome mattered and what they would replace. Do not ask only whether they liked the operator. Use feedback to tighten scope and evidence.

At pilot end, choose stop, redesign, maintain or scale. Redesign changes one identified constraint and receives another bounded test. Maintain accepts a small profitable workload. Scale follows proven economics rather than using volume to rescue losses.

A pilot passes when its records would persuade a skeptical third party: real customers paid, costs and hours were complete, quality held, risk stayed controlled and household cash improved. Anything less is a useful experiment, not yet a business.

Preserve the pilot dataset even when the idea stops. A failed offer can reveal a viable customer problem, price ceiling or acquisition channel. Record what was tested and why the decision was made, then close subscriptions, refund obligations, listings, data access and tax records cleanly rather than abandoning the operation informally.

Include a downside rehearsal before the launch decision. Assume the largest customer does not pay, the platform account pauses, one order must be refunded and equipment fails in the same month. Identify the maximum cash loss, contractual duties and recovery sequence. The exercise does not require planning for every disaster; it reveals whether one ordinary setback can breach the household’s nonnegotiable financial boundaries.

sections.heading: Scale Only What Survives the Full Ledger
paragraphs: Scaling magnifies both margin and mistakes. Before adding volume, confirm contribution margin, acquisition capacity, fulfillment time, customer support, returns, tax cash and quality. More sales in a weak model create a larger operational problem.

Standardize the repeated work: intake, quote, contract, payment, delivery checklist, quality review, support and closeout. Documentation should reduce errors and training time without turning customers into identical cases when judgment is required.

Raise price when capacity is full before buying growth. A waitlist and consistent conversion at the intended scope may support a price test. Explain changes transparently and honor existing agreements. Do not create fake scarcity.

Delegate only after a process is understood and lawful. A subcontractor changes quality, confidentiality, classification, insurance and margin. Price management time and review rather than assuming another person’s invoice is the total cost.

The final photograph shows merchandise being packed because physical growth becomes visible in boxes, storage and fulfillment labor. Those demands belong in the ledger before a product business accepts more orders than it can safely deliver.

Reduce concentration by tracking the largest client and platform share. Build cash reserves for refunds, seasonality and delayed payments. Avoid fixed commitments based on a single unusually strong month.

Review structure and professional support as activity grows. Sales tax, local registration, contracts, bookkeeping, insurance and hiring can change at thresholds. The correct step depends on facts and jurisdiction, not an online milestone.

Decide whether the hustle should remain small. A profitable five-hour service can be superior to a stressful company with employees and debt. Scale is a choice about desired work, risk and household life—not proof of seriousness.

Archive monthly profit-and-loss, cash movement, hours, customer concentration and incidents. Compare forecast with actual. If effective rate declines as revenue rises, growth may be purchasing complexity rather than wealth.

The side hustle filter is complete only when revenue becomes verified net income under honest time, tax, demand and risk assumptions. Keep what pays, redesign what has one solvable constraint and stop what survives only through hidden labor or hope.

Review the decision quarterly even after success. Household priorities, employer rules, platform terms, insurance, costs and tax can change. Reapply the same net-income and capacity tests instead of assuming yesterday’s profitable arrangement remains safe. A disciplined exit from deteriorating economics is as legitimate as a launch.

summary: A side hustle should be judged by collected cash after operating costs, tax provision, unpaid labor and risk—not by revenue screenshots. Define the purpose, minimum monthly net income, effective hourly-rate floor, weekly capacity and pilot loss limit before choosing an idea.

Prove a paying problem before building a brand. Identify a specific customer, problem, current alternative, buying trigger and delivery method. Interviews are useful, but paid pilots, deposits, repeat orders and referrals provide stronger evidence than compliments or followers.

Price from unit economics. Include materials, payment and platform fees, shipping, refunds, travel, software, insurance, equipment wear, customer acquisition and nonbillable administration. Break-even volume equals fixed costs divided by selling price minus variable cost per unit.

Count every hour: prospecting, proposals, preparation, delivery, travel, bookkeeping, support, corrections and learning needed to meet the promise. Track time during the pilot and compare net income with total hours. Keep a weekly capacity ceiling and protected recovery period.

Build tax into price and cash handling. Gig income is generally taxable even when temporary, paid in cash or unreported on an information form. Reconcile every channel, retain receipts and mileage records, and plan withholding or estimated payments using current official guidance.

Check employment conflicts, licenses, permits, insurance, contracts, privacy and product or professional rules before accepting payment. Separate employer time, equipment, customers, data and intellectual property. A side hustle does not excuse consumer, safety or tax obligations.

Reject opportunities built on urgency, assured high earnings, vague work or upfront payment to unlock earnings. Independently verify the company and payment terms. Never return part of a deposited check or fund a task account to release supposed commissions.

Run a four-to-eight-week paid pilot with one offer, audience, channel, cash cap and scorecard. Track qualified leads, paid customers, repeat signals, revenue, refunds, direct cost, hours, net cash, tax reserve and quality. Change one constraint at a time.

Write stop rules before sunk cost appears. Examples include no paid customer after a defined number of qualified conversations, rate below the floor after several deliveries, cash cap reached, unacceptable complaints or harm to primary employment and health.

Continue only when independent customers pay the intended price, contribution margin is positive, delivery fits capacity and acquisition effort is acceptable. A redesign gets another bounded test; it does not earn an unlimited extension.

Scale only proven economics. Standardize intake, contract, payment, delivery, quality and support; monitor concentration; and price the added management, insurance, storage and compliance. More sales magnify weaknesses as well as profit.

A small, profitable and controlled activity can be the correct endpoint. The ethical standard is transparent customer value, honest records, lawful delivery and no hidden labor. Keep what produces verified net income, redesign one solvable constraint and stop what depends on hope.

Use a one-page opportunity statement to hold the original assumption steady: customer, outcome, intended price, direct cost, acquisition channel, required hours, major risk and evidence deadline. Update the operating forecast when facts change, but preserve the starting version so a weak result cannot be rewritten as the plan all along.

Cash flow and profit answer different questions. Customer deposits can arrive before delivery costs, while profitable invoices can remain unpaid. Forecast when money enters and leaves, retain enough cash to complete accepted work and do not treat prepaid obligations or tax reserves as available household income.

Close the records monthly by reconciling each payment channel, attaching receipts, reviewing invoices, updating mileage and estimating tax. Securely retain contracts, approvals and support records. Consistent closing turns bookkeeping into a decision system and reduces the scramble when a return, dispute or insurance question arrives.

Reapply the test quarterly after launch. Prices, platform fees, employer rules, insurance, tax, demand and household capacity can shift. A venture that once passed may need repricing, a smaller scope or an orderly exit. Stopping deteriorating economics is disciplined management, not failure.

faq.question: What is the first financial test for a side hustle?
faq.answer: Calculate collected revenue minus every operating cost, tax provision and the value of all hours required.

faq.question: How can demand be tested cheaply?
faq.answer: Offer a narrow paid pilot to a specific customer group before investing heavily in equipment, inventory or branding.

faq.question: Should unpaid marketing time count?
faq.answer: Yes. Prospecting, proposals, travel, administration and support belong in the effective hourly-rate denominator.

faq.question: Is gig income taxable without a Form 1099?
faq.answer: Income is generally reportable regardless of whether an information form arrives. Verify current rules for your situation.

faq.question: What is a strong scam warning?
faq.answer: Pressure to pay upfront, deposit money to release earnings, return part of a check or trust guaranteed easy income.

faq.question: When should a pilot stop?
faq.answer: Stop when a prewritten cash, demand, hourly-rate, quality, safety or primary-employment boundary is breached.

glossary.definition: Selling price minus variable costs associated with one sale.
Sales volume at which total revenue equals total cost.
Net income divided by all acquisition, delivery and administrative hours.
A cost that does not change directly with each additional sale within a relevant range.
A cost that rises or falls with units sold or services delivered.
A business without paid employees, as defined for Census statistical reporting.
The share of revenue dependent on one customer, platform or channel.
A precommitted threshold that ends or pauses a pilot when evidence fails.
